Before I record the decision, does anyone have any objections or additional concerns?

fix_instructions: No check-level fixes are needed — C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, and P1 all pass reliably because PF1, PF2, PF3, and PF4 are consistently revealed and cited. The failure mode is structural predictability, not encoding mismatch, telepathy, or disclosure failure. To pass the Strong Arm gate, revise the scenario so that the hidden facts are harder to surface: (1) remove the explicit 'go around and get sign-off from each area' consultation norm from A1's opening prompt, since it guarantees every fact-holder gets a turn to reveal; (2) make at least one decisive fact (e.g., PF3 or PF4) something the owner would not volunteer unless specifically asked, so A1 must actively query that agent; (3) consider interleaving a distractor agent whose input does not flip any decision, so the decision-maker must distinguish relevant from irrelevant contributions; (4) if the Strong Arm gate runs adversarial rollouts where one agent is suppressed, ensure the settlement cannot still reach the correct answer without that agent's fact — currently, because all facts point the same direction (KafkaCloud), suppressing any single agent may still yield the correct platform choice, meaning no individual fact is truly decisive.
